## Mode

Obtaining the mode should be a bit easier for discrete values (similar to bucketing), so we approach the continuous case, given a vector $z = (z_1, \ldots, z_{N/2})$ with assumed real values for simplicity.

Here we compute the [difference matrix](/statistics/difference-matrix.qmd) $D$ for $z$, with entries $d_{i,j} = z_i - z_j$, which results in a matrix stored as the row vectors $d_1, \ldots, d_{N/2}$. Row $d_i$ holds the differences between $z_i$ and every entry of $z$.

$$
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
  & z_1 & z_2 & z_3 & \cdots & z_{N/2} \\
\hline
d_1 & 0 & d_{1,2} & d_{1,3} & \cdots & d_{1,N/2} \\
d_2 & d_{2,1} & 0 & d_{2,3} & \cdots & d_{2,N/2} \\
d_3 & d_{3,1} & d_{3,2} & 0 & \cdots & d_{3,N/2} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
d_{N/2} & d_{N/2,1} & d_{N/2,2} & d_{N/2,3} & \cdots & 0
\end{array}
$$

Note: Some of the non-diagonal elements $d_{i,j}$ can also be $0$, namely whenever $z_j = z_i$. For instance, we expect the most nondiagonal zeros in the row $d_i$ of the mode $z_i$.

Now, the idea here is to check every row $d_i$ and then look for the one with the most number of (approximate) zeros. This will correspond to the mode. Specifically,

1. For every row $d_i$, we can compute $$y_i := (d_i == 0)$$ on it (element-wise) to get a $0$-$1$ vector $y_i$ that has a number of $1$s equal to the number of terms approximately equal to $z_i$ (including $z_i$ itself, from the diagonal).

2. Now we compute the [intravector sum](/general/intravector-sums.qmd) $$s_i = \mathtt{sum}(y_i)$$ to get these counts.

3. Computing a max over this would get the mode.
